extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for visual question answering on document images, consisting of questions and answers over varied real document images. It is designed to require understanding of both text and document structure/layout.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Documents were downloaded from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, pages were hand-picked for the dataset, and questions/answers were collected using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage annotation process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Questions deemed inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were flagged and not included in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from 6,071 industry documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning five industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) and many document types.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents used span from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions and answers were collected with remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: (1) workers viewed a document image and defined up to 10 question-answer pairs, with instructions to ask questions answerable from text in the image and to enter answers verbatim; (2) a different worker verified the questions by answering them and assigning one or more question types, with an option to flag inapt questions due to language issues or ambiguity; (3) if answers did not match exactly, the question was reviewed and edited/accepted or ignored by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were reviewed in a third stage when first-stage and second-stage answers did not match exactly; authors performed the final review and could accept edited questions/answers or ignore them.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image; one or more ground truth answers per question could be added.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions and answers were collected in three annotation stages, including verification and review; questions found inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were flagged and not included in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Documents were hand-picked from UCSF Industry Documents Library, with pages prioritized to minimize binarized images and favor pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over running text.

name.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.

description.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images.

url.evidence: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

isLiveDataset.evidence: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset.” “Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool. The annotation process was organized in three stages.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library.”

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: “if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to ﬂag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset.”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “The final set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6, 071 industry documents.” “There are documents from all 5 major industries for which the library hosts documents — tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.”

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: “We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it... Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage... If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage... The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.”

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: “Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage... The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.”

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: “workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted.”

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “The annotation process was organized in three stages... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage... if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text.”
